title: Authored is not delivered
statement: Judge content by what the delivered player shows, checking files, the student's live experience and course claims apart, and count an authored element or gate only once seen working.
example: One course build's feedback was silent, 0/542, and two live courses had a null mastery threshold, so their 90% gate didn't block.
detail: A course quality gate failed one course build with its feedback silent, 0/542, and the course checklist now requires the live response check to return the authored feedback, not the generic fallback, because authored is not the same as resolves. The renderer's notes add that content without proper response processing shows no feedback at all in strict mode. An evaluation of one live course found its 90% mastery threshold declared in metadata but not enforced by any observable mechanism, and a merge found the threshold null on both live courses, so the 90% gate didn't block; the course-fix skill now says to prove a gate with a play-through rather than assert a metadata field as enforced. Check in code that every authored element reaches a surface the student uses, count anything never shown as missing, and count a gate as working only once it is seen blocking.
